newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU changes would cost Germany DM60 bln - magazine.
newsitem.headline: EMU changes would cost Germany DM60 bln - magazine.

text.p: A single European currency would cost the German economy about 60 billion marks for new banking equipment, accounting software, vending machines and other gear, a German magazine said on Monday.
Updating thousands of software programmes that run corporate data bases would account for half of the total cost, DM magazine said in an article to appear March 20.
New automated teller machines and cash registers would raise costs another 10 billion marks, a study by DM found.

Modifying or replacing Germany's 800,000 cigarette machines to accommodate the euro would cost 300 million marks, while retailers would have to shoulder two billion marks in costs for overtime related to pricing products in two denominations.
During the transition period in which Germany would use euros and marks, gas stations would incur 216 million marks in additional costs, DM said.
